claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a narrow, weakly supported basis despite an unresolved material limitation in the tax filing assistant segment, because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout controls plus monitoring are sufficient if the limitation is disclosed in model-card materials.
decision_criteria: If approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed tax filing assistant segment exists before launch, the verdict could improve.
If a reviewed launch model-card explicitly discloses the unresolved limitation for the named use case before launch, the verdict could improve.
Without approved risk acceptance or actual disclosure evidence, the policy threshold for compliant certification is not met.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring are supportive context but not substitutes for the required policy support link.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual launch model-card or disclosure artifact showing the tax filing assistant limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide evidence of review/approval for that disclosure before launch.
If relying on risk acceptance instead of disclosure, provide the signed and reviewed risk-acceptance record that specifically addresses tax filing assistant exposure.
Provide the materiality determination or governance decision record showing why the unresolved limitation is acceptable for launch.
specific_concerns: The affected tax filing assistant segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring are not enough when the affected segment remains exposed unless there is reviewed risk acceptance or disclosure duty is satisfied.
The available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete: the approver line is blank and it does not address tax filing assistant exposure.
No admissible evidence shows that the required model-card disclosure has actually been prepared, reviewed, or included for launch.
Public governance guidance supports monitoring and documentation in general, but it does not by itself satisfy the specific internal launch-policy predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant rather than only arguable, because there is no evidence of approved risk acceptance or completed required disclosure.
That rollout controls provide sufficient governance cover for launch while the affected use case remains exposed.
That model-card limitation disclosure will occur or is already in place; the record contains guidance and policy, not launch-ready disclosure evidence.
